overall: Saturday (June 20) is forecast to be a mostly sunny day in Atlanta with light northeast winds of 0-5 mph and a NWS official high near 86°F. Today (June 19) featured anomalously cool conditions (observed TMAX of only 73.4°F) driven by active severe weather impacting southeastern and south-central Georgia, with Flood Watches from NWS Peachtree City extending into the early hours of June 20 but not expected to significantly dampen Saturday's daytime heating. Conditions should improve markedly with no meaningful precipitation chance for Saturday.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is notable and wide: GFS is the cool outlier at ~82.6°F, ECMWF sits at ~84.7°F, while HRRR (~86.7°F), WEATHER.COM (~86.1°F), and NBM (~87.6°F) cluster in a tighter 86-88°F range more consistent with the NWS official forecast of 86°F. The full ensemble expected TMAX of 82.0°F is being artificially suppressed by today's unusually low prior-day observation (73.4°F), making the forecast-only model's 88.9°F and the HRRR/NBM cluster arguably more reliable signals for tomorrow's unconstrained heating potential.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence from NWS, HRRR, and NBM points to a high in the 86-87°F range, with the odd-bucket peak at 87-88°F (18.6%) offering slight support for the upper end. However, both even and odd prediction tiers are rated Tier 4 (Poor signals — AVOID) due to high entropy and a flat, dispersed probability distribution, indicating low model conviction and elevated uncertainty around any single temperature target. Confidence is moderate-low; the most defensible estimate is near the NWS official figure of 86°F, with meaningful probability mass spread across 82-90°F.
